text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts detected for Private/VPC customers in us-west-2. Metric: net.egress.gateway.5xx > 3.5% over 5m. SEV2. Pager: olivia (oncall). Thread 1976543210.

olivia (oncall): I'm on it. initial triage — how widespread? any customer-facing errors reported yet?

maria (support): two customers reported increases in API retries and 504s around 15:02 UTC. Both are private deployments in us-west-2 using peered transit VPC.

chad (netops): seeing lots of TCP retransmits and RSTs at the egress gateways. Flow logs show many SYNs but few established connections from the return path. looks asymmetric.

sam (infra): pulling route table + peering state now. running quick checks:
```bash
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abcde123" --region us-west-2
aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters "Name=status-code,Values=active,pending-acceptance" --region us-west-2
```

kai (sre2): also check conntrack on the NAT instances and NAT gateway metrics (PortUsage, PacketDrop). NAT gateway cloudwatch shows spikes then health-check flaps.

chad (netops): grabbed a snippet from the transit VPC route table. weird: a recent automation change added a propagation-block route for the peering attachment so return routes aren't propagating to the egress subnets. snippet: 
```
Routes:
 - 10.0.0.0/8 -> local
 - 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-gw-0f1234 (expected)
 # missing propagated routes for peered VPC 172.16.0.0/12
```

olivia (oncall): timeline? when did that automation change run?

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-14T15:00Z: infra/route-propagation: disable-propagation flag set for transit-rt (by pipeline #12877).

sam (infra): that aligns. pipeline changed route propagation at 15:00 UTC — customers started seeing errors at ~15:02 UTC.

maria (support): escalation to customer A and B sent: "We're investigating elevated timeouts; mitigation in progress." they're asking ETA for restoration.

kai (sre2): mitigation plan: 1) revert propagation-block flag via pipeline rollback; 2) add temporary explicit route entries for affected prefixes pointing to NAT gateway; 3) enable fallback routing to hosted inference for critical customers. Which do we prefer first?

chad (netops): revert first — quickest. I can trigger rollback of pipeline 12877 to re-enable propagation. Doing it now.

chad (netops): reverted. route tables show propagated routes coming back. verifying connectivity with curl from a probe instance in the private VPC:
```bash
# from probe host in private subnet
curl -sS -D - https://inference.redwood.internal/health || true
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

olivia (oncall): seeing 5xx% dropping on dashboards already, good sign. keep monitoring for full stabilization.

sam (infra): cloudwatch: net.egress.gateway.5xx down from 3.8% -> 0.6% in the last 4 minutes. Conntrack entries normalize.

maria (support): updated customers: "We rolled back a routing change; service is recovering. We'll follow up with a postmortem and action items." they asked for root cause — will provide after triage.

kai (sre2): root cause draft: automation pipeline inadvertently set a propagation-block flag on the transit route table, preventing peered VPC prefixes from being visible to egress subnets. egress saw SYNs but replies routed incorrectly -> gateway timeouts/5xx.

chad (netops): additional evidence: VPC flow logs showed return traffic for 172.16.0.0/12 hitting a different AZ transit appliance where source-dest checks were enabled and packets were dropped.

olivia (oncall): next steps: 1) open SEV2 incident ticket (I will). 2) schedule immediate postmortem with infra and netops. 3) add pipeline guardrail to block propagation-block toggles without manual approval. 4) notify engineering leads.

maria (support): filing customer impact report now with affected org ids + time windows. will include retries/failure counts.

sam (infra): I'll add a short-term monitor alarm: alert if route-propagation flag changes in transit RTs and a circuitbreaker to pause deploys that touch route propagation.

chad (netops): adding runbook note: if propagation is disabled, add temporary explicit route entries as an emergency mitigation (example):
```bash
aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc123 --destination-cidr-block 172.16.0.0/12 --gateway-id nat-gw-0f1234 --region us-west-2
```

olivia (oncall): handing off to kai for next shift. Kai, you're on for post-incident follow-up and postmortem writeup. I'll close the live paging.

kai (sre2): ack. I'll collect logs, timeline, and owners. leaving a TODO: ensure we correlate pipeline changes to infra alerts to reduce MTTR.

olivia (oncall): closing live paging. If errors reappear re-pager. Great work triaging quickly. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status=Recovering -> Resolved (partial) at 1976543305. Follow-up: postmortem and corrective actions assigned.
